Thank you all for getting these things on the table now — this is exactly why we do these planning calls. Let me work through what I'm hearing and then I'll make my decisions.

First, Ruth — that inspection from Rowan Patel is really valuable. A licensed beekeeper's guidance is exactly the kind of outside advice we need. So we'll follow his recommendations: 12 one-pound jars harvested, 18 pounds left in the hive, and we only take capped honey from the upper super. That gives us our framework.

Eli — three jars promised to the neighbor. I'm not thrilled you committed those before checking with me, but I understand the impulse, and we'll honor it. Three jars to the neighbor.

Caleb — the memorial jar labeled 'Grandpa's Hive' for the family memorial shelf. That's a lovely idea and I'm happy to approve it. One jar, and you'll prepare the label yourself before Saturday.

Mia — thank you for speaking up about the allergy. Safety comes first, no question. You stay at least 30 feet from the hive, on the patio, watching via phone video feed. We'll make sure someone sets that up for you. And please, if you ever have something like this, bring it to me sooner — but better late than never.

So let me lay out the allocation. We've got 12 jars total. Three to the neighbor, one to the memorial shelf — that's four spoken for. That leaves eight jars for the family. I'm thinking we split those evenly among the five of us — that's one jar each with three left over. I'd propose giving the extra three to the households that will use them most. But let me hear from you all — any objections or thoughts on how those remaining eight should be divided before I finalize?
